stem: A leaf shows fine stippling, and close inspection finds colonies of tiny mites plus silk webbing on the underside. Which conclusion best matches the evidence?
choices: The injury proves hemp russet mite because all mites make webbing.
The evidence is more consistent with a webspinning spider-mite problem than with hemp russet mite, while exact species may still require closer identification.
The stippling proves thrips even though no thrips were found.
The webbing can be ignored because only leaf color matters.
rationale: Webbing plus mite colonies on leaf undersides is strong evidence for webspinning spider mites; hemp russet mites do not produce the characteristic spider-mite webbing.
